Kowalski’s research on the corals and the coral reefs of the Pacific Ocean has taken a special interest in the many types of coral reef fishes that inhabit the ocean floor, are often found in the tropics, usually in tropical seas, and are often found along coastal areas where there is abundant water.
“Most of our work focuses on the coral reefs of the Pacific – with some species being able to survive without oxygen,” says Dr. Kowalski. “We also tend to have the shellfish for the fish food. We do not know how much they eat.”
While marine life is highly complex, the scientists say that some organisms are capable of surviving by living on or near the surface of the ocean floor. For example, coral polyps can survive without oxygen from seawater and the ability to grow new shells could help them survive in the absence of oxygen.
“We are very interested in this because it’s so exciting to see how we get to the bottom of the ocean, where we live, when we are exposed to the elements,” says Dr. Kowalski. “The oceans are really rich in iron, which helps them survive without oxygen.”
To learn more about the study, visit the Mycology and Marine Ecosystems website.
